page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data places this instance in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 1585.0 and a multi-core score of 5889.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 425.05 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 56.88 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. However, the instance exhibits performance limitations in specific workloads, such as Redis SET operations which score in the bottom 25% at 7.95 million operations per second, and medium-sized LLM inference which drops to 16.13 tokens per second for prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and compute-focused 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio make this instance suitable for workloads requiring consistent CPU performance without massive memory footprints. It is appropriate for tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight text or image processing. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or larger language model inference due to the lack of local storage, moderate memory capacity, and lower performance in those specific benchmarks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps, with no local storage or GPU accelerators. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, the instance delivers average performance across standard benchmarks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 5889.0 and a static web serving throughput of 11.69 GB/sec. However, it exhibits weaker performance in Redis SET operations and medium-sized LLM inference. Given its 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU resources, this instance is best suited for compute-focused workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, and basic image processing, while being less optimal for memory-heavy databases or large-scale AI inference.
